newsitem.title: GREECE: INFORM LYKOS IN JOINT VENTURE WITH ITALY'S FINSIEL.
newsitem.headline: INFORM LYKOS IN JOINT VENTURE WITH ITALY'S FINSIEL.

text.p: Greece's high-tech printer Inform Lykos said its fiscal 1996 pretax profit rose 8.3 percent to 1.1 billion drachmas on sales growth of 3.6 percent at 5.33 billion.

On an after-tax basis the company expects to post net profits of 715 million drachmas based on preliminary financial results. Inform Lykos invested 1.0 billion drachmas last year and said its debt was nil.

"We expect 1997 will be a better year as our international collaborations and orientation will further contribute to growth. The company will emerge with a new range of activities," board chairman Nick Lykos told a press conference.
He said its new business domain will find itself at the confluence of information technology, graphic arts and communications.

Together with Italy's Finsiel, the company has set up Finsiel Hellas SA where it holds a 49 percent stake. Finsiel which holds the majority 51 percent stake, is a subsidiary of Stet, 78 percent, and the Bank of Italy, 14 percent.
The new joint venture will bring Finsiel's information technology knowhow and experience in state administration, banking and finance to Greece's public sector, Lykos said.

Finsiel with 1996 sales of 1.2 billion dollars employs 8,300 people. Through its subsidiary Sogei it is already working with software developer Intrasoft on the installation of the Taxis software system at Greece's finance ministry.

Inform Lykos also announced a collaboration with AT&T which will focus on Internet commercial applications and EDI aiming to develop a reliable, fast electronic commercial transactions system. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
